headline: India Restores 21.76 Million Hectares of Forest
meta_description: India has restored 21.76 million hectares of deforested land, achieving 84% of its Bonn Challenge reforestation target.
summary_short: India has successfully restored 21.76 million hectares of deforested land, bringing the country within striking distance of its major environmental commitment.
body:
India has restored 21.76 million hectares of deforested land, achieving 84 percent of its Bonn Challenge target. This significant milestone demonstrates the country's progress toward reversing deforestation across its landscapes.

The Bonn Challenge is an international commitment to restore degraded and deforested land, and India's near-completion of its portion shows what sustained restoration efforts can accomplish. With most of its target now met, the country has proven that large-scale land recovery is possible even in densely populated regions facing competing demands for agricultural and development space.

The restoration work represents hope for ecosystems, biodiversity, and climate resilience—transforming not just numbers on a chart, but actual forests returning to the land.
